Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin Test of K Against K + 1 Classes

Source: R/vlmr.R
vlmr_test.Rd

Compares a mixture with one class fewer (restricted) against one with an extra class (full), fitted to the same data, by the likelihood-ratio statistic \(2(\ell_1 - \ell_0)\) referred to the weighted sum of chi-squares of Vuong (1989), as Lo, Mendell and Rubin (2001) proposed for mixtures, and by their finite-sample adjusted statistic \(LR / (1 + 1 / (d \ln n))\), with \(d\) the difference in free parameters and \(n\) the number of cases, referred to the same distribution. It takes any pair of fits compare_mixtures() tests, growth mixtures from fit_gmm() included, so a growth model's number of classes can be tested on fits already in hand. It also takes two latent transition models from fit_lta() that differ by one status, one status against two included, with the same items, occasions and options otherwise (smoothing = 0 and bayes_constants all zero for a published comparison).

Read compare_mixtures()'s section on the test before relying on it: the theorem behind the reference distribution does not hold at the point where the larger mixture reduces to the smaller one, and neither version's p-values are uniform under the null. BIC and blrt() are the better guides. Fit both models without priors (bayes_constants all zero) when the p-value is to be compared with a published one; the test is stated for the plain likelihood.

Usage

vlmr_test(restricted, full, version = c("robust", "standard"))

Arguments

restricted

The model with fewer classes (statuses, for an LTA).

full

The model with one class (status) more, fitted to the same data.

version

"robust" (the default) builds the reference distribution from the sandwich covariance; "standard" from the ordinary one, Vuong's own form (see compare_mixtures()).

Value

A list of class "vlmr_test": statistic (\(2 \Delta\ell\)), df, mean and sd of the reference distribution, p_value, adjusted (the adjusted statistic) and p_adjusted, plus version, ll_restricted, ll_full, n and classes (the two numbers of statuses, for an LTA).

References

Lo, Y., Mendell, N. R., & Rubin, D. B. (2001). Testing the number of components in a normal mixture. Biometrika, 88(3), 767-778.

Vuong, Q. H. (1989). Likelihood ratio tests for model selection and non-nested hypotheses. Econometrica, 57(2), 307-333.

See also

compare_mixtures(), blrt().

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
n <- 400
cls <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
y <- outer(ifelse(cls == 1, 3, 1), rep(1, 4)) +
  outer(ifelse(cls == 1, 1, 0.2), 0:3) + matrix(rnorm(n * 4, 0, 0.7), n, 4)
off <- list(categorical = 0, latent = 0, variances = 0)
f1 <- fit_gmm(y, n_classes = 1, times = 4, random_effects = "none",
              n_init = 5, random_state = 1, bayes_constants = off)
f2 <- fit_gmm(y, n_classes = 2, times = 4, random_effects = "none",
              n_init = 5, random_state = 1, bayes_constants = off)
vlmr_test(f1, f2)
#> 
#> Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test, 1 vs 2 classes (robust)
#> ---------------------------------------------------------
#>   LL: -3120.806 vs -2046.537   2 x diff = 2148.538   df = 3
#>   Reference distribution: mean -3.304, sd 15.688
#>   p = < 1e-04
#>   Adjusted (Lo, Mendell & Rubin): 2035.304, p = < 1e-04
#> 
# }
